definitions.gloss: hand (of cards); cards in one's hand
definitions.explanation: The cards a player is currently holding during a card game or trading card game. Also used figuratively for the options or resources one has available.

examples.japanese: {手札|てふだ}からカードを{一枚|いちまい}{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I played one card from my hand.

examples.japanese: {手札|てふだ}が{少|すく}なくなってきて{焦|あせ}った。
examples.english: My hand was getting smaller and I started to panic.

examples.japanese: {交渉|こうしょう}で{使|つか}える{手札|てふだ}はもう{残|のこ}っていない。
examples.english: I have no more cards to play in the negotiations.

notes:
USAGE:
Commonly used in card games, trading card games, and board games. The figurative use — meaning the options or resources at one's disposal — is also common in business and political contexts, similar to English "cards to play" or "options on the table."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {手札|てふだ}を{切|き}る (to play a card; to use an option)
- {手札|てふだ}を{補充|ほじゅう}する (to draw cards to replenish one's hand)
- {手札|てふだ}が{尽|つ}きる (to run out of cards/options)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {持|も}ち{札|ふだ}: cards in hand — similar meaning; also used figuratively for one's repertoire or resources
- {切|き}り{札|ふだ}: trump card — a decisive card or advantage held in reserve
